title: Combining HTML and ASP
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of combining html and asp in a Classic ASP application.
Identify and describe at least two syllabus subtopics: HTML outside server-side script blocks and Embedding ASP blocks in HTML.
Inspect a minimal example and define a reproducible normal-case and failure-case test.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will study combining html and asp as part of Classic ASP development and legacy maintenance. The lesson follows the attached ASP curriculum topic 35 and uses the syllabus subtopics as the coverage checklist.
content.why_it_matters: Combining HTML and ASP matters because Classic ASP behavior crosses a server-side scripting engine, IIS configuration, request/response boundaries, and often COM or ADO dependencies. A small, explicit test helps distinguish intended behavior from runtime-specific behavior.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Classic ASP templates mix HTML output and server-side script. In 'Combining HTML and ASP', keep presentation readable while ensuring every dynamic value is encoded for its output context. Server-side checks are authoritative; client-side JavaScript can improve usability but cannot enforce access, validate trusted data, or protect database operations.

content_blocks.title: Syllabus coverage
content_blocks.text: The lesson explicitly covers: HTML outside server-side script blocks; Embedding ASP blocks in HTML; Writing dynamic page content; Mixing markup and server-side logic; Maintaining readable page templates. Treat these subtopics as connected requirements. For each one, be able to define the concept, identify where it appears in a Classic ASP application, and name one test or diagnostic that would verify it.

content_blocks.title: Inspectable example: Combining HTML and ASP
content_blocks.expected_output: The static paragraph and dynamic heading are combined in one HTML response.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Keep server blocks short so the template remains readable. The standard CodeLeaf browser playground previews HTML/CSS/JavaScript only; it does not execute Classic ASP, VBScript, ADO, IIS commands, PowerShell, or SQL. This block is therefore marked for static inspection unless you run it in the clearly identified local tool.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the original sample and test data. Change one condition, input, provider setting, or runtime option at a time, then compare observed behavior with the expected result.
content_blocks.limitations: Not executed during course generation. Classic ASP examples require a configured Windows/IIS environment with the matching ASP scripting engine and any required COM/ADO providers. Provider-specific and IIS-version-specific behavior must be verified locally.

content_blocks.title: Runtime and safety checkpoint
content_blocks.text: Submit requests through a browser to a local/test IIS site. Test missing fields, repeated parameters, session expiry, and a second request; do not infer security from a successful happy path. The source syllabus treats Classic ASP as a legacy maintenance technology, not as ASP.NET or a default choice for new web projects.

content_blocks.title: Guided workflow
content_blocks.text: 1. Start with a minimal local example of combining html and asp. 2. Trace its inputs, state changes, dependencies, and output. 3. Test a normal case, a missing/malformed case, and one permission/provider/runtime failure. 4. Write down the exact expected and observed result before changing another variable.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Create a small, reviewable demonstration of combining html and asp using synthetic data. Include at least one of these syllabus concepts: HTML outside server-side script blocks. State the expected result first, then add one invalid or boundary case and explain how your program should behave.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating legacy runtime behavior as universal.
common_mistakes.why: IIS versions, Windows lifecycle, COM registration/bitness, and ADO providers can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Write down the actual server/provider versions and validate on a disposable test site.

common_mistakes.why: Empty input, missing records, expired sessions, permissions, timeouts, and malformed data reveal different failure modes.
common_mistakes.fix: Add normal, negative, and boundary cases with expected outcomes.

common_mistakes.why: Detailed errors can reveal paths, SQL text, configuration, and component information.
common_mistakes.fix: Keep diagnostics in restricted server-side logs and return a generic message with a reference ID.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming syntax alone proves the application works.
common_mistakes.why: IIS configuration, permissions, COM activation, database providers, and response behavior are external dependencies.
common_mistakes.fix: Run against the documented local test host and record exact evidence.
